claims.text: The initially solid Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles have a metastable single-phase solid-solution structure.
Enhanced chemical complexity in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles creates local variations in interatomic bonding.
Local chemical and bonding heterogeneities create diffusion barriers.
The diffusion barriers suppress atomic mobility during premelting.
Multiple constituent elements produce diverse interatomic interactions.
Diverse interatomic interactions effectively localize atomic bonding and reduce atom mobility.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles have a higher premelting onset temperature than Fe–Ni nanoparticles under matched heating conditions.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles have slower atomic diffusion kinetics during the phase transition than Fe–Ni nanoparticles.
Reduced atomic mobility delays the initiation of premelting and modulates melting kinetics.
The predicted mobility suppression will be observable as delayed structural disordering.
The HEA particles will display elemental redistribution distinct from that of Fe–Ni particles during premelting and melting.
Limited free atomic mobility can influence the formation of mixed five-element nanoparticles more strongly than corresponding binary nanoparticles.
Limited free atomic mobility is the dominant factor governing premelting and melting in 5–20 nm Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
The proposed mechanism may not extend to high-diffusion solution synthesis.
The proposed mechanism may not extend to bulk materials.
The quantitative onset-temperature shift and kinetic differences may vary with local composition fluctuations and synthesis conditions.
The controlled comparison uses Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu and Fe–Ni nanoparticles of matched size under identical heating protocols.
Premelting onset is operationally identified by loss of crystallinity and onset of elemental redistribution.
Rapid EDS mapping can provide atomic diffusion coefficients during the proposed in situ TEM experiment.
Failure to observe a statistically significant onset delay, or observation of similar or enhanced diffusion in the HEA particles, would falsify the hypothesis.
